messages:
Priya: Quick sync — first 90d customer feedback. We have a few recurring asks and a couple of regressions. Need to decide bug vs enhancement prioritization for the next two sprints. TL;DR: prioritize P0 regressions, then high-ROI quick wins. Thoughts?

Dan: Can you drop the specific signals? numbers matter for tradeoffs.

Priya: Thanks — summary: customer A & B hit streaming timeout w/ long prompts (3 reports), customer C filed a correctness regression on reranker (1 report, high severity), several support tickets asking for small UX tweak (6 customers, low severity).

Maria: Support: all three timeout reports are reproducible on latest hosted Canary. Logs point to a KV cache miss pattern. I have raw logs + repro steps.

Alex: UX side — the small tweak (reduce field length + inline hint) is a ~2 day change and reduces support volume in our sample by ~40%. Prototype ready.

Dan: Engineering estimate: fix for KV cache path looks like 3-5 dev days + e2e, might require a model-variant canary. Reranker correctness: needs deeper triage — probable root in tokenization edge-case, estimate 5-8 days.

Priya: Proposed prioritization criteria (for this week):
- Safety/regression first (customer-facing breakages)
- Revenue/ARR impact next (customers on contracts)
- Frequency of tickets (volume)
- Effort / time-to-value (quick wins ahead of long reworks)

Priya: Applying the rubric:
1) Reranker correctness (high severity, affects contract customer C) => P0 triage and fix.
2) Streaming timeouts (3 customers, reproducible) => P0/P1 depending on if a quick mitigation exists (fallback to shorter-seq path).
3) UX tweak (6 customers, low severity) => P2 but high quick-win ROI; candidate for sprint 2 backlog or a patch release if we have capacity.

Dan: Agree. Suggest we try a mitigation for timeouts first: fall back to cached prefix + shorter beams. That could be a 1-2 day config + canary. If that helps, postpone the full KV cache patch.

Alex: +1 for mitigation. If we can ship the config change, design impact is minimal. I can prepare the release assets.

Maria: I’ll consolidate repro steps and attach one-pagers for each customer. Also flag any legal/contract notes for customer C.

Priya: Action items: @Dan — scope mitigation + full fix estimates by EOD Thursday. @Alex — prepare UI patch PR & screenshots for a fast patch. @Maria — compile repros + contract notes. I’ll own the prioritization doc and customer comms.

Dan: Will do. Rough plan:
- Today: reproduce + try config fallback on Canary
- Tomorrow: if fallback works, run load test and schedule canary for Fri
- Next week: full KV cache fix branch if fallback insufficient

Alex: I’ll slot the UI patch in sprint board as quick-win (label: quick-win/ui).

Priya: Quick checklist for triage doc (I’ll create it):
```
- customer_id
- symptom
- first_report_ts
- repro_steps
- impact (SEV/ARR)
- proposed mitigations
- long-term fix estimate
- owner
```

Dan: Nice. Can you add a test signal to the telemetry team for streaming timeouts? I want automated alerts if the fallback toggles on.

Priya: Good call — added to doc. @deploy-bot if we can do a canary, ping ops when ready.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy pipeline ready. Use tag: canary/1748876543-fallback. Runbook: /ops/canary-deploy.md

Maria: One more data point: the UX tweak was mentioned in a recent NPS thread — might be worth bundling with a small comms note if we push a patch.

Priya: Okay — plan set. I’ll draft the triage doc and link it here by EOD. Quick sync tomorrow 11:00 to confirm canary results. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
